text: ABSTRACT
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > ABSTRACT

text: In this paper, five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts, including a new highly efficient through-hole (TH) electroplating leveler, were synthesized from environmentally harmless coumarin compounds. The inhib itory properties of five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts were tested by electrochemical method, leading to the selection of the optimal leveler (C2). The adsorption capacity, adsorption state and adsorption sites of different coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts on copper surface were systematically analyzed, and the reasons for the different inhibition capacity of five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts with different molecular structures were explained. The effect of C2 content on throwing power (TP) was studied, when C2 content was only 0.6 ppm, TP value was greater than 100 %. The adsorption behavior of C2 on copper cathode and the interaction between C2 and other additives were studied by the galvanostatic measurements (GMs). SEM and XRD tests were conducted to analyze the effects of different amounts of C2 on the copper plating surface.

text: 1. Introduction
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 1. Introduction

text: With the continuous improvement of the modern electronic indus try’s requirements for electronic components, the demand for electronic components such as electronic chips that achieve miniaturization and high efficiency has also increased. The realization of high-density interconnection between printed circuit boards (PCBs) through micropore connection is an important means to realize the miniaturization of electronic products, so as to obtain more excellent electrical conductivity and space performance [1–3]. Acid copper electroplating is a key technology for copper interconnects in through-holes (THs), and it is also an indispensable technology in the manufacturing process of PCB. In order to obtain a flat and smooth plating layer and efficient TH filling, electroplating additives need to be added to the electroplating solution [4,5].
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 1. Introduction

text: Electroplating additives are generally divided into inhibitors (generally polyethylene glycol and other polyether compounds, such as polyethylene glycol, polypropylene glycol [6,7]), accelerators (generally containing S–H bonds or S–S sulfonate compounds, such as sodium 3,3′-dithiodipropane sulfonate, bis-(sodium sulfoethyl)-disulfide [8,9]) and levelers (generally N-containing compounds, such as Janus Green B, diketopyrrolopyrrole [10–16]).
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 1. Introduction

text: In the process of copper plating, through the interaction of different plating additives, the microhole can be overfilled. In the current research on electroplating additives, electroplating levelers have attracted much attention due to their irreplaceable properties. The leveler is mainly adsorbed on the surface of TH and inhibits the deposition of copper ions on the surface of TH, but has less inhibition on the deposition of copper ions inside TH, so as to achieve the effect of conductive copper interconnection or bottom-up copper electroplating [17–19]. The current research on levelers mainly includes the research of new leveler molecules (small molecule compounds [20–22], quaternary ammonium compounds [23–26] and macromolecular polymers [27,28]), interaction of different electroplating additives [29] and the effect of leveler concentration on filling efficiency and copper electroplating surface morphology [30]. Among them, quaternary ammonium salts have received more attention as leveler due to their superior leveling performance.
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 1. Introduction

text: For example, Myung JunKim [31] synthesized choline-based quaternary ammonium salt levelers and used them in TSV (Through Silicon Via) electrodeposition copper, Jinge Lv [32] designed and synthesized three water-soluble naphthalimide derivatives (NPI) and used them as levelers for microporous electrodeposition. Van Quy Dinh [33] used sulfonated diallyl dimethyl ammonium bromide copol ymer to fill the TSV bottom-up electrodeposition for 5 min to achieve no gaps. These studies have shown that quaternary ammonium compounds have good application prospects in the field of electroplating levelers, but it is still a difficult task to develop electroplating levelers with small additive amount, good leveling effect and environmental friendliness.
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 1. Introduction

text: In our previous work, we found that the large plane quaternary ammonium salt leveler has more efficient leveling performance than the general quaternary ammonium salts, when the concentration is 0.2 ppm (0.278 μmol/L), a very efficient leveling effect can be achieved [34]. Combining the previous work, and the working principle of the leveler −- the leveler molecules are adsorbed on the copper surface during the electrodeposition process to inhibit the electrodeposition of copper ions [14,34,35], we speculate that ^4, 4-bipyridine can be used to connect rigid planar molecules to synthesize larger coplanar quaternary ammonium salts. If such large flat molecules can be adsorbed on copper surfaces, they have the potential to be effective levelers [15,34]. As a common natural product, coumarins (Fig. 1) are planar compounds with two conjugated six-membered rings, and its ^7 position is relatively electron-rich, indicating that its ^7 position is prone to electrophilic substitution reaction. When a hydroxyl group is present, it is easy to undergo substitution reaction with dibromoalkane, thereby further reacting with ^4, 4-bipyridine to obtain a coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salt.
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 1. Introduction

text: Herein, five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts were synthesized by connecting coumarin-based compounds with pyridine-like compounds, including the first synthesis of large plane dicoumarinbased pyridinium quaternary ammonium salt C2 through a four-step reaction. The results of cyclic voltammetry (CV) test and polarization curve test show that C2 can be used as the preferred leveler. The band gap and electron cloud density distribution of five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts were obtained by quantum chemistry calculation and molecular dynamics simulation, in order to study the relationship between the molecular structure and inhibitory ability of these levelers. The experimental results of TH copper plating show that in a certain range, the content of C2 has a positive correlation with the TP value of TH electroplating, and can make the surface morphology of copper plating layer more smooth, and optimize the orientation of the crystal surface of copper particles. GMs results show that C2 can exert inhibition alone and has strong convection-dependent adsorption (CDA) behavior.
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 1. Introduction

text: C2 has competitive adsorption with SPS, no interaction with Cl -, and synergistic inhibition with PEG to form stable PEG-C2 complexes. This study expanded the application of coumarin derivatives and the design range of electroplating leveler molecules, hoping to provide some reference ideas for the development of more efficient levele molecules in the future.

text: 2.3. Quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics simulation
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 2.3. Quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics simulation

text: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were implemented to calculate the adsorption capacity and the adsorption state of compounds A1 − C2 on copper from a theoretical level. Quantum chemistry calculations were based on DFT, the B3LYP function and def2-SVP basis set. The Gaussian 09 program was used to optimize the species geometry. Vibrational frequencies were calculated to evaluate the nature of the optimized structures at the same level. Next, the contour surfaces of the highest occupied molecular or bitals (HOMOs) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals (LUMOs) were visualized with Avogadro program. Electrostatic potential (ESP) surfaces were generated by Multiwfn and VMD software.

text: MD simulation Based on Copper Surface (111). Material Studio was used to simulate the interaction of coumarin compounds (A1-C2) with the copper surface in MD. The thermodynamic temperature of the MD simulation was 298 K, 1000 water molecules and one coumarin quaternary ammonium salt molecule were placed in the initial configuration of the simulation box. MD simulation was carried out under the forcite module and the COMPASS II force field, with a simulation time of 300 ps.

text: 3.2. Potentiodynamic polarization curve measurements
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 3.2. Potentiodynamic polarization curve measurements

text: The potentiodynamic polarization curves of levelers A1 − C2 were tested. In the test of potentiodynamic polarization curve, the turning point at which the current density rises rapidly represents the rapid deposition of copper ions. This turning point is the polarization potential of copper, the stronger the inhibition ability of the leveler, the greater the polarization potential measured in the initial plating solution, the absolute value of the polarization potential is proportional to the inhi bition ability of the leveler [32,34].
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 3.2. Potentiodynamic polarization curve measurements

text: Six levelers were added to the VMS for polarization curve measurements in Fig. 5a. The results of polarization curve measurements were the same as that of CV measurements, C2 had the strongest inhibition ability, which was much stronger than other levelers. The current density represented by B2 starts to be higher than that of JGB, B1 and C1. The reason for this phenomenon may be that the poor maintenance ability of B2 to inhibit the deposition of copper ions. Once the polarization voltage is reached, the deposition of copper ions is greater than A1, B1 and C1.

text: 3.3. Quantum chemical calculation and MD simulation analysis
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 3.3. Quantum chemical calculation and MD simulation analysis

text: Quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics simulations are effective testing tools for developing new leveler molecules [13,37,38]. In this section, the energy band gap, electron density distribution and adsorption state on copper surface of quaternary ammo nium cations of five coumarin quaternary ammonium salts A1~-~C2 were analyzed by quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics simulations, so as to analyze the reasons for the different inhibitory abilities of five coumarin quaternary ammonium salts.
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 3.3. Quantum chemical calculation and MD simulation analysis

text: Fig. 6 shows the optimization results of the geometric structure and electron cloud density of A1-C 2,. The highest occupied molecular orbitals (HOMO) of A1 -C2 are mainly located in the coumarin region, which means that in the molecular structure of A1-C 2,, the coumarin region is more likely than other regions to give electrons to metal ions, thus forming ligand [13]. The lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals (LUMO) of A1-C2 are mainly distributed in the pyridine/bipyridine region, which means that compared with other regions, the pyridine/ bipyridine region is more likely to obtain electrons from the copperplated cathode, thus adsorbing on the surface of the copper-plated cathode. Compared with the other four levelers, LUMO of C2 was distributed in more areas, and LUMO was also distributed in the coumarin region connected with alkoxy in C2 molecule, which repre sented more adsorption sites on C2 molecular structure.
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 3.3. Quantum chemical calculation and MD simulation analysis

text: In general, a higher E _HOMO value means that a compound molecule has a higher electron-giving ability and a lower E _LUMO value means that it has a higher electron-gaining ability, the adsorption ability of the leveler molecules on copper surfaces can be evaluated by the energy band gap ΔE ( Δ E = E _LUMO - E _HOMO) [26,34]. When the E _HOMO and E LUMO values are closer, the smaller the Δ E, it means that it is easier to adsorb on the copper surface [38].

text: In order to further analyze the adsorption sites on the molecular structure of five levelers A1~-~C 2, electrostatic potential energy (ESP) analysis was performed. As shown in Fig. 7, the red area represents the low electron density area, the blue area represents the high electron density area, and the depth of the color represents the degree of low electron density and high electron density. The main low electron regions of the levelers A1 -C2 are concentrated at sites 3, 4 and 5 of the coumarin structure and the pyridine/bipyridine ring, indicating that levelers A1 -C2 are mainly adsorb on the surface of Cu through the intramolecular coumarin group and pyridine/bipyridine group. This indicates that coumarin structure and pyridine/bipyridine structure are conducive to the adsorption of leveler molecules on copper surface.

text: Fig. 11 shows the cross-section of through-holes obtained after plating with different additive formulations. The thickness of the seed layers is 25 μm and the image of the seed layer (before plating) is shown in Fig. S1. The TP value of “formula a” without any additives was 46.28 %, copper ions were mainly deposited on the surface of the through-hole where the plating solution had stronger convection and more rapid replenishment of copper ions. When PEG 10000 and SPS were added, the TP value increased, but it was far from the effect of a complete copper interconnect. Compared with “formulation a” and “formulation b”, the deposition of copper ions on the though-hole surface was more suppressed, which represents a good leveling effect of C2. The leveling effect increased with increasing concentration of compound C2. When 0.6 ppm C2 were added to VMS (“formulation e”), the TP value reached 102.24 %, which means that the copper ions in the middle of the through-hole are deposited faster than on the surface of the through hole with good filling effect,therefore a complete copper interconnection without voids can be achieved in through-hole electroplating. text: 3.5. Action mechanism of leveler C2
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 3.5. Action mechanism of leveler C2

text: GMs can simulate the convection inside and on the surface of the though-hole during the actual through hole electroplating by rotating the disc electrode at different speeds, and test the potential difference after adding different additives to VMS, so as to analyze the effect of different additives and the interaction between additives. The potential difference between low speed and high speed under the same test conditions is defined as Δη ( Δ η = η _L - η _H) [11,41].
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 3.5. Action mechanism of leveler C2

text: As shown in Fig. 13(a), firstly, the VMS was run in constant current conditions for 1000 s, the potential difference was about 0, indicating that the VMS does not have overfill capacity. The potential decreased rapidly with the addition of PEG, representing the rapid adsorption of PEG, while the potential started to rise slowly with the addition of SPS at 2000 s, indicating that the adsorption of SPS is a slow process and its action rate controlled by its rate of adsorption [42]. At 3000 s, the decrease of potential indicates that the depolarization of SPS is inhibited and there is a competitive adsorption relationship between C2 and SPS. At high speed, the potential immediately decreases, indicating that SPS is rapidly replaced by C2 under strong convection. Δη 1 was greater than 0, indicating that the addition of C2 can improve the filling capacity of electroplating solution, which is consistent with the result of throughhole electroplating.
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 3.5. Action mechanism of leveler C2

text: Fig. 13(b) shows when C2 is added to chlorine-free VMS, the po tential at high speed decreased significantly, and no other additives were needed, indicating that C2 alone can exert copper plating inhibition and has strong CDA behavior, which is beneficial to the occurrence of through-hole overfilling. When C2 and Cl - are added, the potential showed no obvious and steady downward trend, indicating that there was no stable synergistic inhibition between C2 and Cl-. The addition of SPS does not result in depolarization, it can be concluded that the depolarization of SPS requires the presence of PEG. Because the competitive adsorption between PEG and SPS is based on the cathode being polarized to a certain extent by PEG. SPS can achieve depolarization effect by replacing PEG in PEG-Cu + -Cl- complex [42,43].

text: 3.6. Effect of leveler C2 on the surface of copper electroplating layer
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 3.6. Effect of leveler C2 on the surface of copper electroplating layer

text: The surface morphology of the copper plating layer is also the focus of the PCB manufacturing process. SEM test and XRD test can well observe the microscopic surface morphology of the copper plating layer, and analyze the size of copper grains by testing the crystallographic plane orientation of the copper plating layer.
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 3.6. Effect of leveler C2 on the surface of copper electroplating layer

text: The test results are shown in Fig. 14. The surface of the copper plate electroplated with VMS (“formula a”) was very rough, and the copper particle diameter was over 10 μm when the magnification was 5000. Combined with XRD analysis, the crystallographic orientation of copper plating layer is mainly (220) crystallographic plane, which means the size of copper grains is larger and the copper surface flatness is lower. When using “formula b”, due to the presence of SPS and PEG 10000, the copper grains were refined, the (220) crystallographic plane orientation was suppressed, and the (200) and (111) crystallographic plane orientations were dominated, and the copper surface looked much flatter, but there were still some defects.

text: 4. Conclusion
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 4. Conclusion

text: In summary, this study synthesized five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts and, for the first time, investigated their application as novel electroplating levelers in acid copper plating. Electrochemical measurements were used to analyze the copper plating inhibition ability of five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts, leveler C2 with double coumarin structure had the strongest inhibition performance. Quantum chemical calculation and MD simulation show that leveler C2 has the strongest adsorption capacity and the most adsorption sites on copper surface, which is the reason why C2 has the strongest inhibition ability. TH copper plating results show that the leveler C2 has good leveling performance, only need 0.6 ppm addition, can get 103.36 % through-hole TP value. The interaction between C2 and other additives and the mechanism of action were further explored by GMs test. The results of SEM and XRD show that the leveler C2 can make the surface of the copper plating layer smoother and optimize the orientation of the copper crystallographic plane.
section: Synthesis of coumarin derivatives as levelers for Through-Hole electroplating of copper in PCBs and a study on leveling mechanism of optimized leveler > 4. Conclusion

text: In this work, a new coumarin compound was synthesized for the first time and used as an electroplating leveler, which expanded the application range of coumarin compounds and the design field of molecular structure of electroplating leveler. It is hoped that it can be used as the basis for the development of efficient leveler molecules in the future.
